cards.name: Run acceleration with a stick-scaled speed target
cards.summary: The stick gives a 0 to 32 magnitude on a squared curve; forward speed climbs by a base gain minus a small drag proportional to current speed, only while below the stick target, and over-speed is shed by a brake that applies on flat ground only.
cards.behavior: Stick distance is clamped to 64 and the magnitude is 32 times the square of distance over 64, so half deflection gives a quarter of the top magnitude. Each update the target speed is that magnitude limited to the run ceiling. If forward speed is zero or negative the player gains a fixed reverse-braking amount. If speed is at or below the target, the player adds a base gain and subtracts a fraction of current speed, so acceleration shrinks as speed rises. If speed is above the target, a brake is subtracted, but only when the floor normal points up with a vertical part of at least 0.95. Speed is floored at zero. The slope step later clamps forward speed to a hard running maximum. Heading turns toward the stick by a rotation step that blends linearly between a slow and a fast value as speed grows, and a fixed value replaces it while the turbo dash flag is set. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Slope slip trigger and sliding friction
cards.summary: Standing on a floor whose normal tilts past about 70 degrees from vertical starts a slip state; once sliding, a per-surface friction multiplier and a slope push shape the slide, with weak stick steering and a 100 unit speed cap.
cards.behavior: A floor is a slip floor when it is flagged as a slider, when its normal vertical component falls below a threshold, or when it falls below a harder force-slip threshold that also overrides jump permissions. While sliding, a velocity vector is updated each update: the slope adds a push along the downhill direction, friction scales the vector, and the facing turns toward the slide direction at a rate proportional to speed. The stick adds a sideways correction that is rescaled so it only rotates the slide direction and never adds speed. Friction is picked from one parameter set per surface kind (normal, oil, water on flat ground, water on a slope, 45 degree slope, any-surface, slider, riding Yoshi); the friction number itself is raised a little when the stick pushes along the slide. Slide speed is capped at 100 units. The slide ends when speed falls below a stop threshold, except on flagged slip floors where it never stops. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Belly slide dive
cards.summary: The dive button launches the player forward at a speed capped at 48, then lands into a long belly slide that can end in a stop-hop or, when fast enough, a spinning long jump.
cards.behavior: In the air, the action button, when it is not read as the ground-pound command, first sets forward speed to a configured dive speed (default 50) and then enters the dive state, where forward speed becomes that value plus 15 but never more than 48, so the effective dive speed is 48. From a slip landing window or oily goop the same button gives an upward speed of 20 before diving. The dive state steers with the normal air controls and ends on contact with ground (the belly slide state) or, on hitting a wall, rebounds. In the belly slide the player uses the slide friction and the stop threshold for the slide (see the slope card). Pressing jump while sliding starts a short hop with an upward speed of 30 when forward speed is at or under the clash speed, and starts a spinning broad jump when forward speed is above it. When the slide speed falls under the catch stop threshold the player ends in a lost-catch (stand-up) state. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Jump launch impulses from the ground
cards.summary: A plain jump launches with an upward speed of 42 plus a quarter of forward speed and keeps 80 percent of forward speed; the second and third chain jumps use stronger fixed values.
cards.behavior: Jump launch sets the vertical speed to a base value plus a share of the current forward speed, then scales forward speed. The plain jump uses base 42, speed share 0.25 and forward scale 0.8, so a runner at speed 32 leaves the ground at an upward speed of 50. The second jump of a chain uses base 52, no speed share and forward scale 0.8. The third jump uses base 70, speed share 0.25 and forward scale 0.8. The plain jump numbers are fixed in code; the second and third jump numbers come from the jump parameter table. Special floor types replace the plain jump with a floor-defined launch value. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Second and third jump chain window
cards.summary: Landing opens a short window; pressing jump inside it at 20 forward speed or more promotes a plain jump to the second jump and then to the third, otherwise the chain resets to a plain jump.
cards.behavior: After touching down from a plain jump the player enters a landing slip state with a counter. Each update the counter rises; when it reaches the limit the state ends and the chain is lost. If jump is pressed while the counter is below the limit, the state looks at which chain stage it belongs to. In the plain-landing stage it starts the second jump only if forward speed is at least the second-jump speed; in the second-jump landing stage it starts the third jump only if forward speed is at least the third-jump speed; otherwise it starts an ordinary jump. A stick rotation during the press turns the new jump into a spin jump instead. A slip-jump miss (jumping from a slope that forbids jumping) starts a miss-jump instead of a chain jump. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Back flip, turn-around, wall and broad jump launches
cards.summary: Several special jumps use fixed vertical and forward speeds: the back flip from a crouch, the turn-around jump, the wall kick and the turbo-dash broad jump.
cards.behavior: The back flip (crouch plus jump with the plain spray nozzle selected) sets forward speed to -16 and upward speed to 62. The turn-around jump after a sharp reversal sets upward speed to 62 and forward speed to 8, facing the stick. The wall kick sets upward speed to 62 and forward speed to 24 in the new facing (see the wall slide card: other values written just before entering the state are overwritten). The broad jump, available when jumping at near top turbo-dash speed, sets forward speed 80 and upward speed 30; the spinning broad jump out of a fast belly slide uses forward 60 and upward 20. Spin jump launch upward speed is 62 with a quarter speed share. All speeds are in the same units as the plain jump. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Air steering, gravity and fall speed limit
cards.summary: In the air the stick adds a push along and across the facing, forward speed decays slightly, gravity pulls 0.8 per update down to a terminal speed of 75, and a spin jump falls with lighter gravity.
cards.behavior: Every airborne update first multiplies forward speed by a drag close to one. With a stick input, the stick component along the facing is added to forward speed with a control gain, and the component across the facing becomes a sideways speed with a second gain; the raw stick magnitude (0 to 32) multiplies both. Forward speed above 32 loses 0.2 per update and speed below -16 gains 0.4. Horizontal velocity is rebuilt from forward and sideways parts and clamped to a maximum horizontal speed of 80. Gravity subtracts 0.8 from upward speed per update; during a spin jump it subtracts 0.6 once falling. Upward speed is never below -75. When the jump button is no longer held and upward speed is above 20, upward speed is multiplied by 0.75 per update (variable jump height; the held-button bit meaning is inferred). Caution on the two control gains: the slip-jump variant of this function scales the stick by 1 over 32 before using the same gain, but this function does not, so a gain of 0.5 would add up to 16 speed per update. Treat the 0.5 defaults as unreliable and tune air steering by feel; the shipped value is in a parameter file that is not in this repository. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Spin jump from a stick circle
cards.summary: Rotating the stick through all four quadrants while jumping starts a spin jump that launches higher than a plain jump, twirls the model and falls with lighter gravity.
cards.behavior: The controller keeps a short history of stick angles. The detector marks which of four angle bands the history has visited (beyond plus or minus 24576, from -24576 to -8192, within plus or minus 8192, and from 8192 to 24576) and needs all four. The result is a right spin when the angle history is mostly rising and a left spin otherwise. A jump starting or continuing under this test switches to the right or left rotate jump. The spin jump launches with upward speed 62 plus a quarter of forward speed and keeps 80 percent of forward speed, turns the model by 4096 binary angle units per update (a full turn every 16 updates), and, once falling, uses the lighter spin gravity. Source note: the quadrant flags look uninitialised in the decompiled form, so exact detection may differ in the shipped binary. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Wall slide and wall kick
cards.summary: Hitting a wall at speed above 16 starts a wall slide that hangs for 20 updates and then slides faster each update up to 30; pressing jump kicks off with an effective upward speed of 62 and forward speed of 24.
cards.behavior: The wall slide state keeps a timer that is capped at 60. For the first 20 updates velocity is zeroed so the player clings in place; after that downward speed is the timer times 0.5, giving at most 30 units. Each update the player is pushed a step into the wall along the wall normal so contact is kept. If the wall plane disappears or the ground is reached the state ends in a landing. Jump at any time inside the slide runs the wall kick, which flips the facing half a turn and enters the wall jump state. The kick function first writes an upward speed of 52 (or 1 if the head would pass within 160 units of a ceiling), but entering the wall jump state runs the shared jump-launch routine, which overwrites vertical speed with 62 and forward speed with 24. The effective kick is therefore 62 up and 24 forward, and the 52 and ceiling-clamp writes are dead. Running into a wall while pressing jump takes the same path: it writes 52 up and 50 forward and then the launch routine replaces them by 62 and 24. Entering the slide needs forward speed above 16 on contact, so slow contact only stops the player. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Wall impact outcomes by speed
cards.summary: A head-on wall hit in the air is resolved by forward speed: above 50 a knock-back, above 16 a rebound into the wall slide, and without a wall plane a knock-back at 38 or more.
cards.behavior: An airborne hit within a clash angle of head-on (default about 75 degrees either side) reports a wall hit. The checks run in this order. Above the clash speed (50) the player takes a knock-back fall with a hit effect (not during a wire roll jump). A wall flagged no-wall-jump drops the player to a rocket-landing state. A fence is grabbed. Above 16 forward speed the player reflects, flips the facing and, if a wall plane is known, enters the wall slide with a camera shake. With no wall plane, speed of 38 or more gives a short knock-back, speed above 8 sets forward speed to -8 and lands, and anything slower stops horizontal motion. On the ground, running into a wall above the clash speed also gives the knock-back. Since running tops out at 32 to 45, the clash speed is reached only through dashes, slides or other boosts. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Ground pound with a wind-up and a super pound
cards.summary: The ground pound hangs and spins in place for up to 60 updates, then drops at 50 units, becoming a faster super pound at 80 after 50 updates, with a 250 unit hit radius.
cards.behavior: The state starts with a wind-up where the player has no horizontal speed, a zero attack radius, and a small upward drift during the first 40 updates of a timer that counts toward 60. When that timer reaches 60 the drop begins. During the drop, upward speed is fixed at -50. After a counter passes 50 the pound becomes a super pound with upward speed -80. During the drop the attack radius is set to the ground-pound radius of 250 and the attack height is 50, so the pound hits targets within a wide ring. On contact with ground the player sends a hip-drop message to the ground actor (a super-pound also sends the stronger message), shakes the camera, spawns particles and ends. Hitting a wall instead gives a short back knock. Source note: the 60 and 50 counts apply to the state counter, whose update rate is unverified. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Hard landing damage and stomp bounce
cards.summary: Falling more than 1000 units at a downward speed above 70 with the water pack on makes a heavy landing that costs 1 health; stomping an enemy bounces with an upward speed of 30, then 40, then 50 on consecutive stomps.
cards.behavior: A landing counts as a hard landing when the drop from the recorded start height exceeds the fall height, the vertical speed is below -70, the player is not on Yoshi and the floor is not a soft type. Only a player carrying the water pack (and not using the underwater nozzle) takes the damage path: a body tremble, a stumble landing state, a rumble, a sound and a floor damage of 1 health. Without the pack the hard landing changes nothing except sand sinking. A stomp on an enemy sets upward speed to a step value plus a quarter of forward speed and cuts forward speed to 80 percent. The step follows the stomp animation: the first stomp uses step one, a stomp while that animation is still playing uses step two, and a third and later use step three. A broad jump stomp turns into a back jump instead. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Airborne collision probes and head clearance
cards.summary: The jump step looks ahead by a quarter of velocity, probes walls at two heights (150 and 30 above the target), a floor from 30 above the target and a ceiling against a body height of 160.
cards.behavior: Before moving, the jump step builds a target position a quarter of the velocity ahead. It checks two wall heights: a chest probe 150 above the target and a low probe 30 above it, each with the player radius. A floor probe starts 30 above the target; if the target is below the floor the player is placed on it. A ceiling probe starts 80 above the old height and pushes the player down when the 160 unit body height would pass it, zeroing horizontal speed and any upward speed. A wall seen only by the low probe (not the chest probe) while the hang option is enabled makes a ledge hang test. A wall at either height sets the wall plane and, if within the clash angle of head-on, reports a hit. Overall, the player behaves as a roughly 160 unit tall body. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Nozzle slots, swap and the tank amount
cards.summary: The water pack holds six nozzle slots, swaps between the spray nozzle and one saved second nozzle over ten updates, and keeps the tank as a fraction so a swap keeps the same fullness.
cards.behavior: The slots are spray, rocket, underwater, Yoshi mouth, hover and turbo; each has its own parameter file, including a tank maximum. The pack starts on the spray nozzle with the hover nozzle saved as the second choice and a full tank. A swap request moves a progress value toward 0 or 1 by a step each update (default 0.1, ten updates); the nozzle actually changes when progress crosses one half. On change the pack computes the used ratio of the old tank and stores the same ratio of the new nozzle maximum, so swapping never refills. Diving-map stages refill the tank each update, and the Yoshi slot is always full. Getting hit drains a per-nozzle damage loss from the tank. Source note: the tank maximum and damage loss are shown as constructor defaults; shipped values are in the parameter files. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Refilling by sucking up water and draining while firing
cards.summary: In water the held trigger pulls water back into the tank at a rate proportional to the trigger level, and firing in water with a full tank is free; outside water each emitted drop removes tank units at the nozzle drain rate.
cards.behavior: The trigger level is the analog trigger reading mapped through three thresholds, then multiplied by 150 to give a pressure. In any water, while the player is not on Yoshi, the pack adds pressure times the nozzle suck rate to the tank each update and plays a suction sound; shallow pool water also lowers the pool level. In water, when the tank is full and the player is pumping, the pack fires and the tank is reset to full every update, so spraying in water costs nothing. Outside water, emitting removes the number of emitted drops times the nozzle drain rate; with no water left the nozzle stays off. Several nozzles use a drain of zero in the constructor and rely on the parameter files, so use the numbers here only as an outline of the formula. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Spray nozzle output scales with a trigger level
cards.summary: The spray nozzle blends drop count, speed, size and damage between a minimum and a maximum by a trigger level that is scaled by 10 and clamped to 1, and each shot pushes the player back.
cards.behavior: The nozzle builds a ramp that follows the trigger target by a fixed rate each update, and uses the gap between target and ramp as the output level. The level is multiplied by a scale of 10 and clamped to 1, so it saturates at full strength with a small gap. Drops per update, shot speed, drop size and attack strength are each a straight blend between their minimum and maximum by this level; the drop count carries a fractional remainder between updates so low levels still fire. Firing pushes the player backward by a reaction speed blended by the same level and projected on the facing, and adds an upward push from the emit direction times a vertical reaction (both zero in the constructor and set by parameter files). Forward speed gets the push through a helper that caps it at 99. Source note: from this function alone the level reads zero once the ramp has caught the target, so how a steadily held trigger keeps firing is not confirmed here. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Charged shots for the hover, rocket and turbo trigger nozzles
cards.summary: Charged nozzles fill an inside pressure of up to 4500 at 150 per update times the trigger level, minus a leak of 100 per update, then fire for a short burst and need a full release before the next charge.
cards.behavior: While the player is pumping and has water, the pressure gains 150 times the trigger level each update, and loses 100 every update. At a full trigger the net gain is 50 per update, so with the default maximum of 4500 the charge takes about 90 updates; below a level of two thirds the pressure can never rise. At the maximum the nozzle enters its active state for the trigger time (default 1 update), plays a sound and rumble, and emits drops, with count, speed and attack blended by pressure over its maximum. After the burst the nozzle enters a dead state with pressure zero and stays there until the trigger reads exactly zero. Underwater a nozzle with less water than its tank maximum cannot charge. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Hover nozzle: lift to a target height
cards.summary: While the hover nozzle sprays in the air, upward speed is set each update to 3 percent of the gap to a target height 160 above where the hover started, with horizontal speed damped by 0.95.
cards.behavior: The hover state begins when the current nozzle is flagged as a rocket type, the player is pumping and the nozzle is emitting. The target height is the current height (or the floor, when started from the ground) plus the hover height. Each update, upward speed becomes the gap to the target times the accel rate, so the player rises smoothly and settles near the target with a time constant of about 33 updates; forward speed is damped by the brake. Stick input adds to forward speed with the diving control gain (0.02) when the stick is mostly along the facing, and turns the facing when it is mostly sideways; the two nozzle models tilt to match. The state ends when spraying stops or water runs out, going to a rocket landing. A ceiling clamps the height. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Rocket nozzle lift comes from recoil, not a height lock
cards.summary: Only the hover nozzle has a target-height rule in the player code; the rocket and turbo nozzles gain height through the vertical recoil of their emitted water, and a rocket height default of 1500 exists but is never read.
cards.behavior: Each firing update adds an upward speed equal to the negated vertical emit direction times the emit speed times the nozzle vertical reaction, and a forward push as in the spray card. The code of the rocket state sets an upward speed of 10 on entry, and the jump state check that triggers it accepts any nozzle flagged as a rocket type. Because the vertical reaction default is zero in the constructor and the shipped value lives in a parameter file that is not in this repository, the actual climb speed of the rocket nozzle cannot be read from the source; use a game-design value instead. The rocket height field in the pack parameter table has no reader anywhere in the source, so it is dead data and should not be treated as live behaviour. The camera in the tower mode tilts up while the player is rocketing. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Turbo dash ramp and broad jump
cards.summary: Holding the turbo trigger ramps a dash speed by 0.5 per update to 32, then waits 120 more updates before the dash flag engages and forces the run speed to 60; jumping at that speed does a broad jump.
cards.behavior: While the turbo nozzle is selected, the player is pumping and the trigger is held with water left, a dash speed rises by 0.5 per update up to a plateau of 32 and is used as the stick magnitude (so the player runs even with no stick input, facing forward). Once at 32 a timer counts up; after the start time (default 120 updates) and when the nozzle is actively spraying, the dash flag turns on. While the flag is set and the player is running, forward speed is forced to the dash maximum of 60, with a spray sound, and pressing jump at 59 or more starts a broad jump. When the trigger is released the dash speed multiplies by 0.8 per update until it falls under 0.1, and the flag clears. Hitting a wall or leaving a run or swim state resets the timer and flag. Total build-up is about 64 updates to the plateau plus 120 updates. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Water particles: a 256 slot pool with gravity and actor hits
cards.summary: Spray is simulated as up to 256 particles, each pulled down by a per-type gravity (default -0.4 per update), ended on hitting an actor, a water surface or a pool, and limited in horizontal speed by its own size.
cards.behavior: A request to emit stops when the pool of slots is full, and returns how many particles it started. Each update, a particle with a hit radius tests hit actors; a successful sprayed-by-water message ends the particle, plays a splash sound and sometimes spawns a splash. Horizontal speed is capped just under the particle size so fast particles do not tunnel. In flight, gravity is added to vertical speed and the position moves by the velocity; a particle sliding on a surface replaces its velocity by a friction-damped drift along the plane normal; some modes simply fall along the plane. Reaching a water surface ends the particle with a small ripple and sound; a floor splashes and shrinks the particle by a magnify factor. Seventeen particle type parameter files (one per nozzle mode) give each type its own extension, magnify, clean size, gravity and lifetime; the numbers here are constructor defaults. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Goop floors: slip states, oil friction and damage clocks
cards.summary: Standing on goop turns running into an oily run whose velocity is multiplied by 0.98 each update (0.99 when sliding), lasting up to 600 updates after the last goop contact, and harmful goop deals 1 damage after 240 updates of contact.
cards.behavior: For the slip, instant-kill and safe goop kinds the goop layer is sampled on a 3 by 3 grid of points 32 units apart centered on the player, and the player counts as dirty only if all nine points are polluted. While the player stands on goop the dirty timer is refreshed to its full value every update; after leaving goop the oily motion lasts until the timer runs out. In an oily run the player cannot steer normally: velocity gains a stick push of 0.01 per magnitude unit and is multiplied by the oil brake each update; when the timer ends the brake becomes zero and the velocity dies. A floor normal at or below 0.99 turns contact into an oil slope slide instead. A damage clock starts at yellow time plus red time (240 plus 600) and decrements while standing on goop; when it reaches the red value (after 240 updates) the player takes 1 damage, and the clock repeats every 840 updates. Fire goop damages at once if the player is within a height of 1000 above the floor, with a knock-back and invincibility. Electric goop damages after a short grace period. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Cleaning goop with spray and shedding dirt
cards.summary: Water particles hitting a floor clean a disk of size 12 times 10, or 12 times 32 on walls; spraying with the plain nozzle also erases 4 disks of size 400 in front of the player; swimming and spin jumps shed dirt.
cards.behavior: Every water particle that lands on a floor or wall shortens its own lifetime and calls the goop manager to clean at its position. The size is the type clean size times 10 for the floor and times 32 for walls. Separately, while the plain spray nozzle emits, the player cleans four times per update a disk of size 400 centered 200 units in front. The goop manager implements clean as a stamp of type zero. Dirt on the player rises while running (0.1), catching or sliding on goop (0.3) and slipping (0.2), and falls while swimming (0.5), after leaving water (0.2) and in a spin jump (0.1), up to a maximum of 200. cards.name: Surface swimming with buoyancy and a floor
cards.summary: Swimming adds stick-scaled forward speed with no drag, applies a gravity of 0.1 against a buoyancy that grows with depth up to 120 and damps vertical speed by 0.95, so an idle swimmer floats about 12 units below the surface.
cards.behavior: Each update forward speed gains the stick magnitude times 0.8 divided by 32, multiplied by a brake of 1. The turn rate between a slow and fast value is a linear function of forward speed. Vertical speed gets gravity of 0.1 downward plus a buoyancy equal to the depth below the surface divided by the float height of 120, clamped to 0 to 1, times a buoyancy factor (both factors 1); idle waiting uses the wait factor and moving uses the move factor. Vertical speed is then multiplied by 0.95. With these defaults the buoyancy equals gravity at a depth of 12. The player is kept at least 35 above the floor. When the water is shallower than the end depth of 80 the swim ends and the player stands. Pressing jump with the water pack dashing at the surface launches a broad jump; otherwise at the surface with a neutral stick, a wall in front or a reversed stick it leaves the water with a plain jump, and otherwise it paddles. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Health, and the air meter that stands in for health underwater
cards.summary: Health defaults to 8 hits; underwater the air meter, not health, takes damage and heals, draining 0.001 per update and refilling 0.03 per update at the surface.
cards.behavior: Normal health is clamped by the health maximum. While under the surface, or wearing the diving helmet, damage and healing change the air meter instead of health; running out of air (below 1) triggers the loser state and a swim-down. The air meter is measured in health units, with its maximum set from the starting health plus one. Each update underwater it drops by an air rate (the helmet uses a second rate, equal by default), and above the surface it rises by the air increase rate up to the maximum. A drop across a whole unit gives a rumble and a short invincibility. The head must be below the surface by the breath depth before it counts as underwater. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Orbit camera driven by a single pitch ratio
cards.summary: One 0 to 1 ratio sets both camera pitch (about 5 to 55 degrees) and distance (450 to 2000); the vertical stick changes that ratio by 0.01 per stick unit and the horizontal stick orbits the yaw.
cards.behavior: The camera sits on a sphere around a look-at point 133.4 above the player. The vertical stick changes a ratio (clamped between a low and high limit), and both pitch and distance are linear blends of their minimum and maximum by that ratio, so pushing the stick moves the camera along a smooth arc from low and near to high and far. The horizontal stick adds yaw at a rate that also blends by the ratio (both ends 250 by default). Field of view is 50. Each camera kind (follow, wall jump, aiming and others) has its own table with these fields. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Camera chase rates, jump pan and transitions
cards.summary: Camera position and look-at chase their targets by fixed fractions per update (0.04 and 0.08 for position, 0.1 and 0.03 for look-at), the look-at drops 100 while the player is airborne, and mode changes blend over 16 updates.
cards.behavior: Camera position moves toward the wanted position by a fraction of the gap per update: 0.04 horizontally and 0.08 vertically, and the look-at moves by 0.1 horizontally and 0.03 vertically, so the vertical focus lags. While the player is not touching the ground the look-at height offset chases a value of -100 at 20 units per update, which pans the view down on jumps. When the right stick is in use and the player moves, the position chase blends toward a faster value of 0.3 (horizontal and vertical) according to how far the player moved that update, capped at 20 units. Camera mode changes (follow, wall jump, ground pound, rocket jump, wire and others) blend over a period of 16 updates in the defaults. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Camera wall, floor and ceiling guards and pitch limits
cards.summary: The camera is pushed out of walls that come within 80 units, kept 144 above the ground (30 while aiming), held 60 below ceilings and limited to about 87 degrees of pitch, with a slope tilt of up to 8192.
cards.behavior: A wall check pushes the camera out whenever a wall plane is closer than the check radius of 80, scaled by a revision ratio (1 by default). The ground check keeps the camera at least a clearance above the floor; the clearance blends from 144 to 30 as the player readies the water pack. The ceiling check holds the camera 60 below a roof. The polar chase keeps a minimum horizontal distance of 300. The final pitch is clamped to plus or minus 15872 binary angle units (about 87 degrees). On slopes the camera samples the ground 50 units ahead of the player and tilts up to 8192 binary units, chasing the tilt at 50 per update, and ignores slopes steeper than that. While aiming, extra horizontal distance is added, 350 at the lowest pitch shrinking to 0 at the highest. The value is the built-in default written in the parameter constructor; the game then loads a parameter file from its disc image that may replace it, and that file is not in this repository.
